overview: CS4290 is the Capstone check flight. The discussion should prove the student can brief any prior maneuver and any emergency procedure as an integrated mission problem, then adapt to real-time contingencies without inventing procedures or losing the recovery picture.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion Items

items.text: Any previously discussed maneuver on the check flight is not a request to dump every prior event. It is a prompt to show a repeatable brief format and apply the right procedure to the actual scenario.

children.text: State the maneuver purpose, entry setup, airspeed, altitude or area requirement, configuration, and clearance or formation contract.
Brief execution, completion cue, common error, and the condition that requires reset, terminate, knock-it-off, missed approach, or recovery.
Tie the maneuver to the profile: formation departure or rejoin, high work, instrument approach, missed approach, holding, divert, or recovery.
Formation scenario: depart on separate clearances, rejoin in the working area, conduct radial rendezvous, split or rejoin the flight, or manage a section emergency.
Instrument scenario: fly a published missed approach, accept a different approach after ATIS, handle unplanned holding, or navigate point-to-point.
Navigation scenario: fly a leg without the TSD when airspace and flight plan permit, using backup navigation and cross-checks.
Weather or fuel scenario: recognize when simulated weather, divert suitability, holding, fuel, or approach changes should replace the original plan.
Use current 1801, route packet, SOP, IFG, weather, fuel, NOTAMs, and day-of brief for local execution details.
A strong answer explains how the plan changes, who needs to be told, and what must be verified before continuing.

items.text: Any emergency procedure on CS4290 is a check of recognition, memory items, N/W/C interpretation, and recovery judgment, not a challenge to invent a list of emergencies.

children.text: Cue: identify the malfunction or emergency from indications, aircraft behavior, environment, or formation context.
Control: protect aircraft attitude, airspeed, altitude, terrain clearance, and formation separation.
Action: execute required memory items, then use the checklist and N/W/Cs to choose the correct branch.
Recover: decide whether to continue, divert, PEL, forced-land, fly a missed approach, coordinate section support, or eject.
For a single-aircraft emergency, state the aircraft-control target, memory item, checklist/N/W/C, field or ejection decision, and radio plan.
For a section emergency, state lead transfer, perch, detach, lost sight or blind separation, and who coordinates with ATC or tower.
For IMC or approach emergencies, state safe altitude, clearance or emergency authority, lost-communications assumptions, missed approach, and suitable recovery field.
For weather divert or damaged-aircraft cases, state field suitability, runway, fuel, crash crew, approach options, and whether the flight should remain joined.
Do not brief a scenario-specific contingency as universal procedure unless the controlling source says so.
When the emergency creates a conflict with the planned check-flight profile, the emergency recovery plan takes priority.

items.text: Any Previously Discussed Maneuver and Any Emergency Procedure

studyNotes.summary: CS4290 should be studied as the cumulative Capstone check: use a disciplined maneuver brief, apply emergency procedures through N/W/C-driven decision branches, and adapt to real-time contingencies with current source verification.

summary: CS4290 covers cumulative maneuver review, emergency-procedure decision flow, and real-time contingency management for the Capstone check flight.
title: Capstone Check Flight
